newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Afghan Talebans arrest and beat Argentine reporters.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Talebans arrest and beat Argentine reporters.

text.p: Two Argentine television journalists have been arrested as spies, beaten and robbed by the Taleban Islamic fundamentalists who control Kabul, their employers and Argentine officials said on Thursday.

Their television channel Telefe said war correspondents Natalio Aides and Walter Moor, both Argentine nationals, were detained by the new rulers of the Afghan capital on Wednesday, a day after they arrived on a United Nations flight.

Argentina's U.N. Ambassador, Fernando Petrella, said in letters to the United Nations asking for help that the pair were "detained on charges of espionage, apparently either at the U.N. offices or at the Hotel Continental in Kabul."

"They were beaten and their work equipment, video cameras etc, confiscated by the Talebans," Telefe said in a statement. Its news department spoke with them earlier on Thursday and found them "concerned about their situation and the abuse to which they have been subjected."

The Taleban has imposed stern Islamic Sharia law since taking over Kabul three weeks ago. They control three quarters of Afghanistan but the government they ousted is fighting back and ex-defence minister Ahmad Shah Masood has given them an ultimatum to quit the capital or face the consequences.
